research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; current CSEW quality, sample design, coding, weighting and production assurance; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Crime in England and Wales QMI output contract
verified_claims: the QMI was last revised on 2 April 2026
outputs can be accredited official statistics or official statistics depending on source and measure
the statistical bulletin is produced quarterly
limitations: designation must be attached to the specific measure rather than the whole publication
quarterly publication does not make every input quarterly

sources.name: CSEW collection scale
verified_claims: the CSEW is a face-to-face survey
the design covers around 31,000 people aged 16 or over
a separate survey covers around 1,500 children aged 10 to 15
limitations: survey counts are not crime-event counts
children and adults use different instruments and must not be pooled without method metadata

sources.name: CSEW recall and household scope
verified_claims: respondents are resident in households in England and Wales
the survey asks about experiences in the 12 months before interview
the instrument is a victimisation survey
limitations: recall period differs from police-recording dates
household residence excludes institutional and business populations

sources.name: CSEW excluded crime and population scope
verified_claims: CSEW does not cover crimes against businesses
it excludes people not resident in households
it excludes homicide and victimless offences such as drug possession
limitations: excluded offences must not be treated as zero
coverage advantages apply only to included crimes and populations

sources.name: CSEW response-rate quality statement
verified_claims: the provisional response rate for year ending March 2025 was 46 percent
this was substantially below historical rates
ONS reports that its quality review found little impact on reliability of headline estimates
limitations: a headline quality conclusion does not eliminate subgroup nonresponse bias
response-rate statements require survey-year versioning

sources.name: CSEW achieved sample for 2024 to 2025
verified_claims: the adult target sample was 31,000 interviews
31,532 adult interviews were achieved
1,437 children aged 10 to 15 took part
limitations: achieved counts do not imply equal precision for every subgroup
adult and child samples require separate weighting

sources.name: CSEW police-force-area minimum design
verified_claims: the sample design targets a minimum of 585 interviews in each police force area
smaller police force areas are oversampled
PFA sample design supports area-level precision objectives
limitations: a PFA minimum does not create LSOA or parcel estimates
oversampling requires design weights

sources.name: CSEW sampling frame
verified_claims: the core sample is drawn from the small users Postcode Address File
ONS describes the PAF as the accepted general-population sampling frame
the design represents households and people living in them
limitations: the PAF frame does not include every non-household population
an address frame is not an exact parcel-boundary source

sources.name: CSEW victim-module structure
verified_claims: the first three victim modules contain detailed incident questions
the last three modules are shorter
the shorter design is intended to reduce respondent fatigue
limitations: module position can affect information depth
repeat incidents require dedicated methodology

sources.name: CSEW offence coding
verified_claims: specially trained coders determine whether a reported event constitutes a crime
coders assign the applicable CSEW offence code
coding is based on processed adult and child victim modules
limitations: survey coding is not police crime-recording classification
coder decisions require the applicable coding-version context
